key_idea: The river is a functional graph; reverse it and DFS from every sink and every cycle while maintaining a multiset count of the sightseeing spots adjacent to the current root-to-node path.
sketch: Each river cell points to the next river cell or to nothing (land or outside). In the reversed graph every component is a tree hanging from a sink or from a cycle. DFS down the reversed edges: on entering a cell increment a counter for each adjacent spot (tracking how many spots have a non-zero counter), on leaving decrement; the number of distinct spots when standing at a cell is exactly the answer for a trip starting there. For a cycle, first add the spots of all cycle cells (every start in or above the cycle traverses the whole cycle), then DFS into the non-cycle children of each cycle cell. O(r*c). Pitfalls: a spot adjacent to several path cells counts once, the DFS must be iterative (depth up to 250000), and the land cell where the raft stops contributes nothing. Stress-tested against direct simulation.
